title: Moving from paper to digital
text: I was looking for a better way to manage my daily to do list and discovered Reminders on my iPhone. I spent a block of time learning how to input to do items, appointments, meetings and tried that for several weeks. I learned that I could also track credit card cycles, including posting dates and due dates. After 3 weeks of transitioning from paper to digital, this has really freed up a lot of time writing out and updating manually. I learned that I can set up recurring reminders and then when I mark the items as completed they appear one month later automatically. These sync to my iPad, iPhone and MacBook so I can check the list from any of my shared devices.

title: Some missing functionality leads to “bloating.” Customizability sometimes lacking in easy-fix places
text:
Reminders has a cornucopia of good features, but then has shortcomings that discourage using them.

The “hourly” repeat is an excellent feature if you need to remember to do something on the hour. However, it lacks the “pick-and-choose” ability like with weeklies that allow you to pick “M-T-F-S” or any other combination, meaning you have to manually check off hourly 8 times in a row to shift the next reminder to the morning, otherwise your smart watch will buzz every hour (several times if you have several hourly reminders) likely waking you up in the middle of the night.

The way the default folders work is confusing, but I suppose can be learned.

The new “urgent” reminder feature is nice, though I’d really prefer to be able to customize the snooze duration to be 10 or 15 minutes instead of 9, since the 9 minute snooze is a vestigial feature that came from how physical analog clocks/watches worked. It’s not inherently bad, it definitely has its purpose to avoid two reminders going off at the same time, but it should be an option rather than the default.

(Also I apologize if I’m getting you mixed up with Timer, but I’d also really prefer that Bluetooth not be bypassed, it’s rather embarrassing for a user in a quiet room in public to realize that the sound that’s been playing over their AirPods/ headphones for the last 10 seconds was masking the sound of it also playing out loud on their phone’s ringer.)

That’s all I can think of off the top of my head (I’m writing an in-app review so I can’t look over the app once more before submitting this), also thanks if you read this whole thing, took me a little while to write it.

Hoping that this & the new urgent reminder feature means the team is keeping an eye on reviews & still open to making changes/ adding new features 😁. Just wanted to end by pointing out the changes I suggested are risk-free so long as they’re a supplement/ new option rather than a replacement.

Thanks for all the work put into this, despite all the ways I think it could be even better, I still use it every day :).

title: Reminders has evolved into a truly useful app
text:
Once upon a time I stopped using Reminders. It didn’t seem to have the persistence or the functions to truly breakthrough and remind me of important things. 
But now because Reminders has so many different features and the ability to store an image with your reminder as well as set an alarm for that reminder on your iPhone (instead of just popping up and disappearing) I use it heaps. 
One of the most useful things is the image. 
One way I use it is with online grocery orders for click & collect. I take a snapshot of the order confirmation screen so I have the order number, collection date & time. Makes it very easy to set the reminder because the information is IN the reminder screen not buried in a different app plus Reminder also shows up on my calendar as a time commitment which is astonishingly useful. I pre-booked a paid parking bay through an app the other day and it required a code be input when entering the car park, so a screenshot of that went into the reminder at the date and time for when the car park booking commenced so it was already popped up as a reminder on the lock screen of my phone when I arrived at the car park and a couple of clicks I had the code to put in the keypad for entry. 
A big well done to the planners & developers that have evolved Reminders to what it is now. 😁

title: A few basic features to add
text:
The app works well, but is missing a few simple features that would make it a lot more user friendly. When you add things to your schedule there is are different sorting options, and even though one says manual, it doesn’t actually let you change the order. They are only based on time or priority, but I use the app simply for to do lists really for my days, so would be nice to just drag and drop to reorder, without having to add times or anything like that. It still would give people the option to use the other features of it, but making it easier to use for those only using it as a simple to do list app. You can already do this within lists, just no option for the schedule which is honestly the main part I feel! Also in terms of to do lists, other apps have a “someday” option, where you can add things to days, then add things you need to do but don’t have a day set yet. I did just make a separate list for this, but would be great to have the option to see it in the weekly schedule. Lastly the option to have completed tasks once ticked move to the bottom of your list for that day. Definitely should be an option to turn on or off, as there would be plenty who would prefer it this way, but plenty who like it as is. It is possible in your own list, but not in the weekly schedule. So having an option that we can choose what suits would be great! Honestly as I’m only using it for to do lists and not actually reminder notifications, there are better apps out there but I just love that this being an Apple app integrates so well with siri and my Apple Watch, I would really love it if it had some of these features to make using it as a simplified to do list simpler.

Edit to add - I love the shopping list automation where it adds to categories. But eggs are not dairy, come on. I know from TikTok that there’s some weird thing where in America people are convinced they are dairy because they are in the same supermarket section, but the rest of the world knows better, so eggs automatically going there is silly. The heading “dairy, eggs & cheese” that is automatically one of the headings is silly because cheese is dairy, you don’t need to specify both. So I changed it to just dairy and eggs still go to that section. lol. Would be nice if you could rename your sections to suit and it worked seamlessly. I used to just use notes for my shopping list and my headings were based on the local supermarket I use and were ordered for the aisles so it was easier to tick off once there. I tried renaming my sections but it’s not quite smart enough to be able to place items correctly, and keeps making new headings. Eg. I created a “bakery” section, but when I add “bread” it automatically creates a new “breads & cereals” section. I get why that’s a section, you know based on dietary guidelines, but they are in different sections of the supermarket (in my country) so I don’t really want them to be together. Anyway I am just making do with the automatically created sections, but feedback for future updates!
